metadata.case_name: TANG KA WAI ALEX v. CHAN WAI KIN

plaintiff.occupation_before: Quantity surveyor (employed by Leighton Contractors (Asia) Ltd)
plaintiff.occupation_after: Quantity surveyor (employed by Leighton Contractors (Asia) Ltd)

injuries.description: Neck injury (cervical spine) treated with internal fixation and posterior fusion (C3/4) with bone grafting and wiring; tenderness over the cervical spine; no neurological deficit reported.
source: He received internal fixation for his neck which was immobilised with a collar for a month.
A physical examination at the hospital indicated tenderness over the cervical spine, with no neurological deficit.
He was operated in respect of his neck injury and an open reduction posterior fusion with bone grafting and the wiring of C3/4 and was performed for the neck injury.
Dr Au found that the neck injury resulted in a body impairment of 25%.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of other specified cervical vertebra

injuries.description: Left knee injury: 8-cm deep laceration with some bone loss; knee sutured; some mild limitation of left knee action; muscle wasting at left calf noted.
source: He also suffered an 8-cm deep laceration over the left knee with some bone loss.

It is noted in his follow-ups at Prince of Wales Hospital that there was some neck and left knee pain and that neck movement were almost full and that there was some mild limitation on the left knee action.
Dr Au found that the muscle wasting at the left calf, as a percentage of body impairment was 2%.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of lower leg

injuries.description: Psychological injury: post traumatic stress disorder and persistent neck pain with avoidance behaviours; claimed inability to drive a motor vehicle following the accident.
source: In addition to the damage caused to the neck and to the left knee, the plaintiff claims a psychological impairment in that he now is unable to drive a motor vehicle.

"Mr Tang suffered from post traumatic stress disorder and persistent neck pain. He had frequent flashback and avoidance behaviours. He was vulnerable to hyper-arousal when he passed by the scene of the accident.
Though he maintained his work as a quantity surveyor, he found it increasingly stressful as he still had fear to drive to different outdoor sites…."
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain, stiffness or tenderness only

manifestations.description: Two to three episodes of neck pain a day, each episode lasting about one minute; neck pain increases in rainy weather.
Becomes tired easily after the injury and needed rest after working for about an hour.
Episodes of left upper limb numbness occurring once a week and lasting for about one minute.
Left knee pain occurring in the morning when getting out of bed; jogging causes left knee pain.
Neck movement almost full (noted on follow-ups), lateral flexion to right 40 degrees and to left 30 degrees; rotation both right and left 60 degrees (as recorded by Dr Au).
Some mild limitation on the left knee action.
Muscle wasting at the left calf (assessed as 2% body impairment).
Avoidance behaviour and fear of driving; attempted driving in a car park but unable to cope mentally.
Frequent flashbacks and vulnerability to hyper-arousal when passing by the scene of the accident.

treatments_received: Immobilisation with collar for one month
Open reduction posterior fusion with bone grafting and wiring of C3/4
14 sessions of arthroscopic examination and orthopaedic treatments
Psychological outpatient clinic sessions (4 sessions at Pamela Youde Nethersole Eastern Hospital; 3 sessions with psychologist Nadasa Liu)
treatments_future: Ongoing follow-up physiotherapy and arthroscopic/orthopaedic treatment
Estimated 10 sessions of arthroscopic and orthopaedic treatments (future)

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Some reluctance to drive; claimed inability to drive a motor vehicle after the head-on collision leading to avoidance behaviours and fear of driving to outdoor sites.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Plaintiff was a Karate enthusiast before the accident but had not been a serious participant in competition for some time; injuries are a factor but did not loom large in damages calculation.
Neck movement limitations (lateral flexion right 40 degrees, left 30 degrees; rotation 60 degrees) and neck pain affecting movement.
Mild limitation of left knee action and left knee pain affecting mobility.

In addition to the damage caused to the neck and to the left knee, the plaintiff claims a psychological impairment in that he now is unable to drive a motor vehicle. "Mr Tang suffered from post traumatic stress disorder and persistent neck pain. He had frequent flashback and avoidance behaviours. He was vulnerable to hyper-arousal when he passed by the scene of the accident. Though he maintained his work as a quantity surveyor, he found it increasingly stressful as he still had fear to drive to different outdoor sites…."
